subject: Iterate across rows of parameter values for a population model

messages.author: 4b0fc25b7336801c
messages.subject: Iterate across rows of parameter values for a population model
parts:
Hi D-RUGies,

I am trying to figure out if it's possible to efficiently use a data frame of parameter values as inputs to a function that runs a population model.  Ideally, the solution would use tidyverse functions.  I was trying to use the function map() across a list of nested data frames, but it's clear that R can't figure out that the variables are located within each data frame (see the error below in red).  I'd like to get the value of N.fished out of the population model function, and have it attached to each nested data set somewhere.

Attached is the data RF_parms.  Here is the code:

library(tidyverse)
library(purrrlyr)
library(purrr)

RF_parms <- read.csv("~/RFparmsforMEGAFUNCTION_LY.csv")
RF_parms.list <- RF_parms %>% 
    group_by(Species) %>% 
    nest() 

#1. Function to model population
openpop_time = function(df) { 
  df %>%
  a_harv0=(log((Lfish-Linf)/-Linf)/-k)+a0  
  agefish=round(a_harv0,digits=0) 
  N0=rep(100,maxage)
  N0[1]=R
  s=exp(-M)
  sf=exp(-(M+Fi)) 
  sfx=rep(sf,maxage-1)
  sfx[1:(agefish-1)]=rep(s,(agefish-1))
  sxs=rep(s,maxage-1) 
  Nt = matrix(0,tf,maxage)
  Nt[1,] = N0 
  t<-1

  for(t in 1:(tf-1)) {
    Nt[t+1,1] = R
    Nt[t+1,2:(maxage)] = sfx*Nt[t,1:(maxage-1)] 
  }
  
  N.fished=Nt[tf,]
  return(N.fished)
}

RF_parms.list2 <- RF_parms.list %>% mutate(N.fished = map(data, openpop_time)) 

Error in mutate_impl(.data, dots) : 
  Evaluation error: object 'a0' not found.

Any insight would be greatly appreciated!  Thanks for your time.

Lauren

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Iterate across rows of parameter values for a population model
parts:
Lauren, 

Your first problem is that your function is not working. 

You are piping df into a_harv0=(log((Lfish-Linf)/-Linf)/-k)+a0

I think you mean to put this into a mutate(), but many parts of your function wouldn't go into a mutate call unless you save them as a list in a list column. N0=rep(100,maxage)

I think the advice I've seen is to filter your parameter values and isolate the first row. Then use that as your input to your function and make sure it works. Then you can use map to iterate over the parameters. 

That said, I've seen pmap used in many examples for this sort of thing. Perhaps that would be better used here? Hard to say since I don't fully see what you want your function to do. 

HTH, 
B

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Iterate across rows of parameter values for a population model
parts:
I haven't looked at your specific code here, but for a higher level view and some code examples of 'how to work with rows' in the tidyverse, take a look at this talk by Jenny Bryan https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/thinking-inside-the-box-you-can-do-that-inside-a-data-frame/
and the materials for it https://github.com/jennybc/row-oriented-workflows

As you'll see if you do look, there are a lot of different ways to do something like this in the tidyverse and it seems the "best practice" way to do this is always changing (I've had this problem before  https://stackoverflow.com/questions/36345558/using-standard-evaluation-and-do-to-run-simulations-on-a-grid-of-parameters-wit ;). That said, it seems the best way to do it has involved a purrr function with 'map' in its name for a while, including pmap which Brandon mentioned.

- Jaime

messages.author: 44eb106d2d552f20
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Iterate across rows of parameter values for a population model
parts:
Thanks very much, Brandon and Jaime!  This is amazing.  Naming all the inputs in the function was key, as was not piping the data frame to a_harv0, and removing any parameters that were not used by the function.  Not sure why I thought piping a dataframe to a variable would work in the first place!  If I made each of the parameters a list and then gathered them all in a named list called parms, then I could easily pipe the parms list to the openpop_time function with pmap.  Jaime - I can definitely appreciate the problems incurred by changing best practices in the tidyverse.  I have plenty of code that no longer uses a 'deprecated' form of mutate.  


#### Some relevant code parts
RF_parms2 <- RF_parms %>% select(-Species, -Lmat, -Fi.1) 

tf <- as.list(RF_parms2$tf)
maxage <- as.list(RF_parms2$maxage)

# parms as named list
parms <- list(tf = tf, maxage = maxage, Lfish = Lfish, M = M, Fi = Fi, Linf = Linf, k = k, a0 = a0, pW = pW, qW = qW, R = R)

N.fished <- parms %>%
  pmap(openpop_time)
####

Thanks again!
Lauren
